- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md:283-289 | severity=high | confidence=5

  WHY: G4 never fires and held heals stay stuck, and the scan still logs a normal `scan` outcome, so the failure is silent. Severity is MAJOR in all five reviews.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md:266 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: P1 step 5 appends every qualifying linked run to `runs=` with no cap, but `_heal_scope_marker_shape_ok` (scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:3618-3622) rejects more than 3 runs.
  WHY: The marker is reported `malformed`, intake skips with `scope_marker_unresolved`, and no heal is filed, which is a regression. The plan also has no cap test.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md:169,290-293 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new `rescope_scan` origin rebuilds a `workflow_run` heal report from an issue body, but the plan specifies no report-authentication path. The existing gate (scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:407-416) and `reconstruct_recovery_payload` (scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:3920-4013) are bound to the autofix shape.
  WHY: An implementer must invent a trust path and may weaken the #6559 report-authentication gate. Anthropic rated it MAJOR with confidence 3.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md:85,176-177,297,309 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The §27 constraint "No workflow file grows. Any workflow edit is limited to env switch plumbing." contradicts P3 step 4 and P4 step 3, which add env lines to workflow files.
  WHY: Read literally, it makes an implementer skip the plumbing, so the switches are unreachable and the rollback path fails. The real limit is the 480,000-byte guard. Severity disagreement: minimax rated it MAJOR, the others NIT.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md:146-148,348 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The reference-extraction lookbehind permits a preceding `/` and the candidate is always built as `scripts/<group1>`, so the "no further `/`" check can never fail. `scripts/lib/x.sh` resolves to `scripts/x.sh`.
  WHY: The planned test "a nested path (dropped)" cannot pass, and nested references can resolve to the wrong top-level file.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md:71,262 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Provenance rule 4 needs the job that mentioned the linked run, but `--parent-log-map` `{linked_run_id: [parent_run_id, …]}` carries only parent run ids.
  WHY: The window check degrades to the union of all failed-job windows of the parent run, which over-accepts.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md:260 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: P1 step 2 persists the parent run as `${LOG_DIR}/run-<id>.json`, but intake already writes `${LOG_DIR}/run-${run_id}-info.json` (scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1583).
  WHY: Following the plan creates a redundant copy that can drift from the verified one.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md:302 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: P4 step 1 cites an existing sibling-import fallback in scripts/clarify_github_facts.py:38-47, but that file imports only stdlib modules.
  WHY: A bare sibling import can fail under isolated `-I -B` Python invocations and break clarify's facts step.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md:286 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The P3 criterion "with no open PR referencing the issue" has no data source in the reused listing, and the plan claims no per-issue read beyond the recovery path (§15 constraint, line 81).
  WHY: The check is either dropped silently or needs an out-of-budget call, so a heal with an in-flight PR could be replaced. Anthropic's confidence was 3.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md:144-148,302-309 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: For PR-owned heals `scope_ref` is the PR head SHA (scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:3036), and the plan has no deny-list or ownership guard on closure seeding.
  WHY: A PR author's pipeline-control scripts could enter the frozen edit scope.

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Each behaviour has its own default-on switch, and switching it off restores today's output byte-for-byte (Goal G6)
  expected_change_site: Plan §27 constraint and P3/P4 env plumbing
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: §27 "No workflow file grows" forbids the env plumbing in P3 step 4 and P4 step 3, so the switches cannot be turned off and G6 is not implementable.
- requirement: Add one paragraph to the decision rules of `prompts/_templates/mode-clarify-respond.txt` and `prompts/mode-clarify-respond.txt`, and to the question rules of `prompts/_templates/mode-clarify.txt` and `prompts/mode-clarify.txt`, with identical text in each pair (P4 step 2)
  expected_change_site: P4 implementation steps 1-4; scripts/clarify_github_facts.py import of `HEAL_SCOPE_RE`
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The "existing sibling-import fallback pattern" for `HEAL_SCOPE_RE` does not exist in scripts/clarify_github_facts.py:38-47, which imports only stdlib modules. The plan never says whether to inline, copy or add a fallback.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md: P2 step 4 and Constraints "Scope integrity" | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Hardening note. If `scope_ref` is `HEAD_SHA` for PR-owned heals, a PR author's unchanged pipeline-control scripts can enter the frozen edit scope through the closure. The plan has no deny-list or ownership guard.
  WHY: The closure names only files already present at the scope commit, but the edit surface could still widen to shared pipeline scripts.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md: P3 step 1 vs scripts/workflow_failure_heal_recovery_scan.sh line 187 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The jq filter drops every issue whose body carries the scope marker, which is exactly what P3 candidates must carry. The plan never says the filter changes.
  WHY: The rescope candidate set is always empty, G4 never fires and held heals stay stuck, silently.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md: P1 step 5 and G1; scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py `_heal_scope_marker_shape_ok` lines 3618-3622 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The marker shape check requires 1 to 3 runs, but the plan appends every qualifying linked run with no limit and no budget split.
  WHY: More than 3 runs makes `check-marker` report `malformed`, intake skips with `scope_marker_unresolved`, and no heal is filed.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md: "Reference extraction" lookbehind and P2 test "a nested path (dropped)" | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The lookbehind does not exclude `/`, so `scripts/lib/x.sh` matches `x.sh` and resolves to `scripts/x.sh`. The "no further `/`" check can never fail.
  WHY: The planned nested-path test cannot pass, and nested references can resolve to the wrong top-level file.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md: P3 step 1 "no open PR referencing the issue" vs §15 constraint | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The plan lists no data source for the open-PR check, and the reused GraphQL listing returns no linked PRs.
  WHY: The check is dropped silently or needs a call outside the budget, so a heal with an in-flight PR could be replaced.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md: Provenance rule 4 and P1 step 3 `--parent-log-map` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The map carries only parent run ids, so the job that mentioned the link is lost.
  WHY: The window check collapses to the union of failed-job windows, which is looser than the stated rule.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md: P1 step 2; scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh line 1583 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The plan names `run-<id>.json`, but intake already writes `run-<id>-info.json`.
  WHY: Following the plan literally writes a second, redundant copy that can drift.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md: P4 step 1; scripts/clarify_github_facts.py lines 38-47 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The file imports only stdlib modules and has no sibling-import fallback to reuse.
  WHY: A bare sibling import can fail under isolated `-I` invocations and break clarify's facts step.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md: Approach → "Re-check (Q5: A)", P3 scope and step 3; scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh lines 407-416 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The plan adds a `rescope` mode that rebuilds a `workflow_run` heal report from an issue body but does not say how it passes the report-authentication gate (#6559).
  WHY: Without a specified trust path, an implementer may relax the origin gate for `rescope_scan`.
- docs/plans/heal-scope-linked-runs-script-closure-plan.md: Constraints "§27" vs P3 step 4 and P4 step 3 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: "No workflow file grows" contradicts the steps that add env lines to workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml and orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml.
  WHY: An implementer may skip the plumbing, leaving the switches unreachable and rollback ineffective.
- TASK COMPLETENESS / INTENT GAPS: none reported.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS (2): (1) At P1 step 3 and Constraints rule 2, have `linked-scope` pass the run's own `repository.full_name` as `repo` after the case-insensitive check, since `verify_run` may compare case-sensitively (heal.py:7122, 7134, unverified). (2) At P2 step 4 and Risks, skip closure seeding for PR-owned heals or exclude pipeline-control scripts from `closure_paths`. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
